Definition: a departure (from striking the tents), i.e. march (not necessarily a single day's travel); by implication, a station (or point of departure)
BiblicalUsage: The word names a journey, a departure, the breaking of camp, and it is the word of Israel's wanderings. Abram went on his journeys from the south to Bethel, where his tent had been at the beginning, and all the congregation journeyed from the wilderness of Sin after their journeys, according to the commandment of the LORD. When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys, and they took their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every journey in Scripture is a picture of the Christian life, because we do not settle, we follow the cloud. I hold that the God who ordered every departure also ordered every rest, and the journey ends where He pitches the tent, not where we choose to stop.
